title: YouTube Demonetized Me | Rappter Rant
description:
As of a few days ago, I am no longer making any money from my channel through Google AdSense, thanks to a surprise demonetization notice from YouTube. Rooster Teeth is not responsible for this (to my knowledge), YouTube is. I sent an appeal video, and they rejected it within hours. According to them I have large amounts of "reused content" on my channel, even though all of my videos fall within their monetization guidelines as they are written (including reaction videos). Either way, YouTube has neglected to notify me which videos and what aspect of those videos are responsible for this, meaning that reapplying to be monetized again 3 months later likely would not be successful as I do not know what I would need to "fix".

YouTube's various guidelines and customer support systems have always been very flawed, but I am truly shocked by how hard YouTube tries to avoid being specific in any regard or actually working towards a solution. I don't know what out of my content has rustled their feathers, and when I ask them for clarification or confirmation, they ignore me and deliberately remain vague, for no good reason I can come up with. I'm not against admitting that I've made a mistake or done something wrong that would have caused this, but even if I did, the fact is that YouTube has not allowed me to know exactly WHAT I did wrong. That's not acceptable.

Is this the universe's way of balancing things out for me after Stitch VS Rocket Raccoon happened on DEATH BATTLE? Who knows. But this has happened, and I just wanted to let you guys know. Thanks for reading and watching.

transcript: This is not the video I thought I would be making in 2026. The plan for thisyear was to make a comeback to YouTube and post at least one or two videos amonth. My channel reached 70,000 subscribers over the new year. So, I wasreally excited to be making videos again. As you know, there is a lot ofuncertainty at the moment around software engineering with AI making abig impact on the number of jobs available. So, I wanted to see if it waspossible to make some additional money with side projects and to show peoplethe steps needed to get your projects from idea to revenue. With that in mind,I set up a limited company last year to release all of these new products underand I'm in the process of migrating everything to be under this new company.Now, one of these things is my YouTube AdSense income. The amount right nowisn't huge. I make between £100 and200 pound a month, but I was hoping it wouldgrow as my channel would grow and I would start making more videos again.Unfortunately, Google had other plans. Now, Google don't let you just convert apersonal AdSense account to a business account. You have to create a new onethrough YouTube Studio. So, I set up a new Google account owned by my business,then went into YouTube Studio to create the AdSense account and link my channelto it. I went through all the identity verifications and everything looked likeit was fine. I was a bit worried. I have heard quite a few horror stories of thisgoing wrong, but so far it looked good. At least I thought so. The next morning,I get an email from YouTube saying my partnership with them had been disableddue to invalid click activity. Now, I've never had any problems with invalidtraffic in the past, and there's nothing on my YouTube analytics to suggestanything's suspicious or wrong. I have a slight increase in traffic from peoplecoming back to my channel after the holidays, but no more than I usuallyget, which is about 3,000 views a day. I tried to appeal it with their invalidtraffic form. I actually tried twice, but got rejected twice. The crazy thingwith this is they don't tell you anything about where this invalidtraffic is coming from or which videos are getting the traffic or how toprevent it. Even if someone was maliciously clicking on ads to get mychannel demonetized, well done. You've done it if that is the case. It's notlike I can do anything to prevent that. The AdSense email basically says I'mbanned for life from ever monetizing my YouTube channel or monetizing any otherchannels and I won't be able to get any of the AdSense revenue that I earned inDecember, which again it was only £162, but in this economy it's a lot betterthan nothing. So I'm in this weird place at the moment. Do I continue makingvideos on YouTube despite being demonetized and focus on trying to getthings like brand sponsorships or have people support me on Patreon? I shouldsay a big thank you to my three paid supporters on Patreon who are Freddy,Ian, and Joe. Your support really does mean a lot to me. The other option is togive up on YouTube and focus on my blog, my newsletter, and making courses for aplatform that quite frankly actually respects its creators. The thing is, Ido like making videos and sharing my knowledge. So, I would like to keepdoing it, but I would be lying if I didn't say it was a bit demotivatinggetting demonetized. Without that AdSense revenue, no matter how small,it's hard to justify putting in the time it takes to make these videos,especially since I know that YouTube is still likely to put adverts on my videosand make money from all my content. Combine that with YouTube activelypromoting shorts over long form content and all the AI slop that creators nowhave to compete with, it's going to be a hard decision whether to keep continuemaking videos or not. I know from looking at other creators um that are alot bigger than me that AdSense revenue is generally a pretty small part oftheir income. Most of it usually comes from things like brand deals, but untilnow I've been really avoiding doing those because I know people don't likesponsored segments in videos. So, this is where I am at the moment. Ifthis video gets seen enough, then there's a small chance that YouTube willsee it and lift my banan. If not, then I'll have to decide what I want to doand whether making videos is still worth my time and effort. Let me know in thecomments what you think I should do and whether I should carry on making videosdespite being demonetized. Thank you everyone who has watched my videos. Ihope they've been helpful. Whatever I decide, I'm still going to be writing mynewsletter. So, if you don't hear from me on here, then you can sign up to thatvia email or RSS. Thanks everyone. Wish me luck.

title: I GOT DEMONETIZED on YouTube… After Everything I Built
description:
My YouTube channel has been demonetized, and honestly, this is something I never expected to experience.

After putting so much time, effort, and dedication into building this channel and sharing my travel experiences with you, I woke up to the news that my channel was no longer eligible for monetization.

YouTube informed me that my content allegedly violates its sexual content and sexually gratifying content policies. However, I genuinely believe that my videos are about travel, meeting people, social interactions, dating experiences, and documenting real-life moments around the world — not creating sexually explicit or sexually gratifying content.

I have never intentionally created explicit sexual content, and I disagree with the decision. I have submitted an appeal and am currently waiting for YouTube's specialist team to review my channel.

This channel is my primary source of income and a huge part of my life. Losing monetization has put my ability to continue travelling and creating content under serious pressure.

I'm sharing this because I believe creators should be able to understand decisions that affect their livelihoods, and I hope YouTube will carefully reconsider my case.

**If you believe in my content and want to support me, please:**
- Share this video.
- Leave a respectful comment below.
- Help bring this situation to the attention of YouTube's creator support team.

You can tag the official accounts:
X: @TeamYouTube, @YouTube, @YouTubeCreators

I am not giving up on creating content. I simply want a fair review and an opportunity to continue doing what I love.

Thank you to everyone who has supported this journey. ❤️

title: Changes to the YouTube Partner Program & New Ways to Earn
description:
YouTube is updating the YouTube Partner Program. Including revenue sharing for Premium Lite, new Shorts incentives, and updated YPP entry thresholds for ads and premium revenue sharing

Since the YouTube Partner Program launched, the ecosystem has grown massively. There are so many more creators, channels, and formats. And so much more content. To make sure YPP scales, remains sustainable, provides  investment in new creator incentives, and continues to reward active engagement in meaningful ways, YouTube is introducing three updates that will take effect on February 1, 2027

0:00 - Overview of 2027 YouTube Partner Program Updates
0:48 - Premium Light Expansion & Creator Revenue Sharing
1:33 - Shorts Revenue Sharing Updates & New Creator Incentives
2:32 - New YPP Entry Thresholds for Ads & Premium Rev Share
3:12 - What Isn't Changing
3:23 - Next Steps for Creators
transcript: YouTube is updating the YouTube Partner Program, including revenue sharing forPremium Lite, new Shorts incentives, and updated YPP entry thresholds for ads andPremium revenue sharing. Hello, Insiders. I'm Rene Ritchie, a long-timecreator now working at YouTube, and here's what is and isn't changing. Sincethe YouTube Partner Program launched, the ecosystem has grown massively. Thereare so many more creators, channels, and formats, and so much more content. Tomake sure YPP scales, remains sustainable, provides investment in newcreator incentives, and continues to reward active engagement in meaningfulways, YouTube is introducing three updates that will take effect onFebruary 1, 2027. And with these updates, YouTube actually expects to payout even more to creators overall in 2027 than it will in 2026. First,YouTube is expanding Premium Lite to every country where standard YouTubePremium is available. This gives viewers more ways to watch creator contentuninterrupted, offline, and in the background. And more Premium meanshigher potential earnings for creators because, on average, creators earn morewhen a viewer watches via Premium than they do from standard ads. For standardYouTube Premium, creators share in a pool representing 30% of netsubscription revenue, with the rest accounting for YouTube Music Premium andmusic rights. For Premium Lite, because this tier doesn't include the music app,creators share in a much larger pool representing 60% of net subscriptionrevenue. From those pools, revenue splits remain exactly the same, 55% forlong-form and 45% for Shorts. That's YouTube Premium and Premium Lite. Next,YouTube is updating how Shorts revenue is distributed. If you are alreadyearning significant revenue from Shorts, you probably won't notice an impact fromthese changes. Starting February 1, 2027, creators will need to maintain abaseline of 10 million qualified Short views over the trailing 90 days toparticipate in Shorts ads and Premium revenue sharing. If a channel dips belowthat 10 million baseline, it absolutely will not be dropped from YPP, and itslong-form monetization ads and premium will stay completely active. But, tobetter more meaningfully support channels under that 10 million baseline,YouTube is launching new targeted incentive programs. Instead of justrelying on the traditional ads model, smaller and growing channels will havenew ways to earn based on community milestones. This includes things likeYouTube shopping bonuses, targeted incentives for brand deals, earningsboost for participating in and starting cultural trends. And YouTube will besharing the exact opt-in criteria for these new programs soon. That's Shortsrevenue sharing and new incentives. Next, YouTube is updating the thresholdfor new channels applying to YPP for ads and premium revenue share. This does notimpact channels already in the YouTube Partner Program. If a channel is alreadyin, its status stays locked in. Also, the thresholds for fan funding andYouTube shopping are completely unchanged. So, newer channels can stillleverage community support early on. For ads and premium share, for new channelsapplying February 1st, 2027 and on, the new thresholds will be 20 millionqualified Shorts views in the last 90 days, up from 10 million, or 8,000qualified watch hours in the last 365 days, up from 4,000. And those are thenew YPP entry thresholds. To be clear, if a channel is already in the YouTubePartner Program, that channel status is not changing. Revenue splits are notchanging. Fan funding and shopping thresholds are not changing. YouTubeknows that updates to the Partner Program and to monetization are a bigdeal, maybe the biggest deal. That's why YouTube wanted to give creators aheads-up well in advance of the February 1, 2027 rollout. To keep everythingrunning smoothly, the updated agreement terms will be landing in YouTube Studiosoon. All monetizing creators will have 6 months to review and sign the newagreements to continue earning. And there's more information linked in thedescription. So, please, drop your thoughts and questions in the comments,and keep it real.

title: YouTube Partner Program Changes - Explained!
description:
Changes are coming to the YouTube Partner Program (YPP) on February 1, 2027. Creator Insider Rene Ritchie sits down with YouTube VP of Creator Product, Amjad Hanif, to break down all the updates and dive into why YPP needs new entry thresholds and a new 10M Shorts baseline, the brand-new creator incentive programs, and the continued partnership between YouTube and creators

0:00 - YouTube VP Amjad Hanif on Changes to the YouTube Partner Program
0:39 - What Isn't Changing in YPP
0:55 - Why YPP Thresholds Are Increasing
1:42 - Supporting Early-Stage Creators & Fan Funding
2:18 - Minimum Threshold for Shorts Revenue Share & Why
2:51 - New Incentive Programs for Early-Stage Creators
3:30 - Creator Economy Growth and the New Thresholds
transcript: I'm Rene Ritchie, your creator insider. >> My name is Amjad Hanif and I lead thecreator product team at YouTube. >> Thank you so much for joining us. We'veannounced a few updates for the YouTube Partner Program. What is changing forcreators and our channels? >> There's a few changes that most creatorsshould be aware of. The biggest changes are on what it takes to earn from adsrev share. It used to be about 4,000 hours in order to qualify for long formand now it's going to be 8,000. On the short side, it used to be 10 millionviews in 90 days and now it's going to be 20 million views in 90 days.Additionally, in order to earn shorts rev share in the upcoming month, you'llhave to have had 10 million views over the last 90 days. And these are justadjustments based on the amazing growth of the creator ecosystem over the lastseveral years. >> And some things aren't changing, right?>> Yeah, if you are in YPP today, you stay in YPP. What also isn't changing is thefirst level of YPP, which we introduced a few years back called the fan fundingtier. That still takes 500 subs and 3,000 watch hours or 3 million views inthe last 90 days. >> So, let's dive into that a little bit.Why was it necessary to change the thresholds for watch time hours andshorts views? >> YPP stands apart in the entire creatorecosystem and I think it's because of one central element, which is we succeedas a company when creators succeed. And and that's been part of the ethos of theprogram since the first year, 20 years ago till today. And all these changeswe've announced just reflect the reality of an ecosystem that has grown so much.And when you think about it, the kinds of content, the way you consume thatcontent, the formats have all changed exponentially over the last severalyears. And so, we want to make sure that the earnings you get from the programare meaningful and allow you to reinvest in your channel. And all of thesechanges, when you step back, we still expect to pay more out next year tocreators than we will this year. >> For a lot of people, when you ask themlike what they want, what their dream is, it's to be monetized on YouTube,it's to get into YPP. And hope is such a powerful force. How are you thinkingabout that when you're making these changes?>> Yeah, look, it's front and center in our thinking. It is the place where creatorsacross the globe come to earn and build their business. And we've been excitedand proud of the fact that there's over 3 million creators that are part of theprogram. So, the one thing that didn't change is what it takes to join YPP. Itstill takes 500 subs and 3,000 watch hours or 3 million views in the last 90days. And that is a way to think of us reaffirming our commitment to making ita place for creators to start their business.>> Another big change is that now there is a minimum threshold to maintain revenueshare shorts. You have to get 10 million views every 90 days. Why make thatchange and why 10 million? >> It goes back to one of the centralprinciples around these adjustments. Is we want to make sure that the earningsyou get from YPP are meaningful, that allow you to invest and build yourbusiness. Um and we had a case where if you had only a few thousand views, youmight have a few cents for that month. And instead, we'd like to design theprogram in a way where it rewards creators who are leaned in, who aredriving views and engagement. >> And what are you going to do then forcreators who You still want to encourage them to make shorts.>> Absolutely. >> But they're not hitting that 10 millionthreshold. >> Absolutely. So, as a part of this, we'vealso introduced some incentive funds. And so, we've actually quietly beentesting that over the course of the past year. And that's going to give us a wayto target money to creators who are at much earlier stages of their career togive them the boost they need in order to make it to the next level. A simpleincent incentive might be to continue uploading over the next 90 days and earna bonus for that. Um if you've tagged a few items inshopping, we may give you a bonus to tag a few more items in shopping. If you'vebeen able to secure brand deals, you may get a bonus for that. And it allow us tobe much more targeted for creators at those early stages to help them earn toget to that next level. >> The creator economy is bigger than ever.YouTube is doing better than ever. Why aren't we lowering the thresholds forYPP? Why are we instead increasing them? >> That's a really good question. You couldlower the thresholds and you'd have creators who are in the program but notactually earning anything meaningful. There is no program like YPP across thecreator ecosystem. And we take that uh responsibility very seriously asstewards of the creator economy, as the original home for creators to make aprogram where creators can understand what it takes to be part of it, uh canearn based on how well they build an audience. And that's really in the backof our mind with all the changes we make for the program. We want you to be ableto earn and build a business and grow from a business where you're justrunning your channel to one where you can take advantage of brand deals, youcan sell memberships, you can earn from fans directly. And you think of all theways you can earn as a part of the YPP program, there's no other place you cando that today. >> I'm Todd, thank you so much for yourtime. I really appreciate this. I would love to sit down with you again nextyear and see where we've gotten. >> Great, looking forward to it, Rene.>> And you all know what to do. Jump into the comments, leave your questions,leave your thoughts, and keep it real.

Todd,what does your team work on? >> So my team works on a variety of things,but most of it is about recommending content to viewers, uh whether that beon the homepage, on the watch experience, through notifications,and we're really just trying to get the right content to the right viewer at theright time. >> So I went my scour the internet, uhevery nook and cranny, and I was trying to see the most common questions thatcreators had about like {quote} the algorithm. And one that comes up a lotis sort of this idea that I as a creator make a video and then I upload it toYouTube and then the recommendation system, the algorithm, pushes that outto varying degrees of success. title: YouTube Partner Program cancelled, everyone gets demonetized

I am making this video after many and many attempts at getting in contact with YouTube and trying to restore my channel and solve the issue, but it seems the situation keeps getting worse, more and more channels are hit with the same issue, and YouTube demonetized my other channels that are not even related to Pivot Master, taking away a good portion of my livelihood for no reason, so I feel the need to speak out about this. And others should too!

I already tried appealing, deleted some videos with millions views that included humans, and got rejected anyway. I don't mind making adjustments to my channel, but YouTube won't tell me what the problem is. With how many other animators being affected by this, I doubt there is a problem on my end, and is probably caused by AI verification, hopefully our channels can be manually reviewed and restored to their previous monetization.

I hope this issue can be resolved for me and everyone else affected.
transcript: Unfortunately, I am making this video because there is a serious problem atYouTube that I think has to be addressed. Around September of 2025,YouTube decided to demonetize my channel without any warning. They claimed thatmy channel involves dangerous or sexualized content involving minors,which is absurd because my channel does not include any minors, let alone indangerous or sexualized content. I started my channel back in 2014 andsince October 2019, I have been consistently posting and never had anyproblems with any of the YouTube's policies. Each animation takes mecountless of hours, weeks, and sometimes months to prepare, creating one frameafter another for thousands of frames per animation. Then the videos are thengo through the process of editing and sound design before finally being postedon YouTube. When you go through my videos, they all consist of the samekaiju dinosaur topics. Some of the videos have the inclusion of humans asbackground characters, however, never minors. I immediately appealed theirdecision, to which they rejected my appeal almost straight away, claimingthat they did a thorough and manual investigation and that they correctlysuspended my channel. Additionally, claiming that the majority of my channelinvolves harmful content involving minors. After I asked them to provide mewith an example, they refused to provide a detailed list or pinpoint toindividual videos. Instead, they doubled down and told me that their decision wasfinal. This however did not stop there. YouTube went ahead and demonetized mysecond channel that mainly focused on behindthe-scene content and shorts.Additionally, recently YouTube demonetized two of my other channelsthat are not related to the kaiju/ dinosaur niche and are completelyseparate channels on their own because they are connected to a suspendedchannel. Keep in mind that they are not connected through email or AdSense. Thismeans YouTube checked my IP location and suspended all my channels that werelogged in from this IP. Despite me being one of the first animators affected bythis problem, I was not the only one. YouTube has done this to many animationchannels in my niche, including Dino Mania, Slick, Blunt Brothers Production,UG Pandi, Gojira Mania, Val Animation, Mosering, and many others. This list ofchannels keeps getting bigger by the day. As more and more channels are beingaffected by this absurd claim, it seems as though YouTube's new AI systems flagsthe channels in the kaiju and dinosaur niche as channels meant for kids orchannels that include minors for whatever reason. I urge YouTube tomanually review the channels and give them back their monetization. The peoplein this niche are all very hardworking, creative, and talented. It is unfair totake their livelihoods away from them over false claims. Thank you forwatching the video and I hope this brings awareness to this topic and somedifference can be

title: Ross's Youtube Demonetization Spectacular
description:
Ross talks about Youtube video demonetization and what it means for his channel, other youtubers, and the future of the world.

0:00 Intro
0:34 what's happening
2:29 how demonetization might work 
3:03 how this can affect other Youtubers 
7:47 how this affects the future
13:04 explanations of this
18:39 are these pod people?
19:30 how this affects my videos
22:12 the big picture view of this

www.accursedfarms.com

EDIT: I forgot to mention that "The Movie" project I'm working on is still on regardless of any of this.

Also for everyone saying to set up Patreon, I don't do that for reasons mentioned in the beg-a-thon video, but I have a donation page at http://accursedfarms.com/donations (it does both monthly or one-time only).  I was hesitant to even bring that up in this video because I'm still treading above water (particularly September), this was more about what a potentially massive change this is from Youtube.
transcript: Hi!This is a video I wasn't planning on making,but recent events have compelled me to.Now, normally I don't like to cover current events,because most news, you're not really gonna care about in 5–10 years.It's only certain stories that leave a real impact.Well, I think this is one of those stories.More so than I first realized.So even if you're watching this years after the fact,I'll try and frame things so this should still be relevant.I'll start in the present, then expand out.So what is happening?Well, the short version is YouTube has unleashed an AI upon its networkto flag videos that it finds so offensive, or extreme,or just covering the wrong topics,that it cannot recommend them to advertisers to place their ads on them.If a video gets flagged this way, it mostly demonetizes them,effectively meaning the creator receives no money.Now, I'm not 100% on the specifics,but there are reasons for that, which I'll get to.Now this has been going on for a while.I was hoping to ignore it,since I've had enough issues with YouTube over the years as it is,but, nope.I can't.This one felt like a bullet whizzing by my head.A few days ago, while uploading a new video,I discovered 53 of my videos had been flagged overnight.They were mostly "Freeman's Mind," my most popular series,and recorded chat sessions I do with fans each monthas a way to answer their questions.Boy, it hated those,which is understandable.As you can see, this is some pretty crazy stuff.This is pure AI logic at work.Something about what you're looking at here,an algorithm has determined is offensive.I mean, it could be me.This could be the computer's way of saying it thinks my face is offensive.Yeah, thanks computer.I mean, hell, I don't know.Maybe it is.But the computer doesn't tell me why the video is flagged, just that it is.In fact, it doesn't even fully do that,but I'm getting ahead of myself.If I just received a message from YouTubetelling me to put a paper bag over my head,or else they're going to demonetize my videos,that would be more helpful than what's happening now.In fact, what YouTube is doing here is so not helpful,it's the most user-hostile move I've seen in a while.I'm impressed.Now, I'm hesitant to say exactly how this works,because I'm not sure anyone knows that,maybe even YouTube.But based on my own research and personal experience,here's a rough chart showing the possible outcomes for a video.As you can see, there's a lot of ways your video can be demonetized now—some with no recourse.There's a lot of random elementsas to whether you can survive demonetization or not.It's a little different for everybody.Google has essentially turned YouTube into a roguelike.Now, I'm not going to be going over all of this,since I'm sure I'm missing details,but there's a few parts that jumped out at me.This new AI isn't that new.According to sources I read, several months back,it was demonetizing videos, and saying everything was fine,and not telling users anything.This reminds me of "Office Space," where they fire an employee,but instead of saying that to his face,they just stop paying him, and act like nothing has changed.'We always like to avoid confrontation whenever possible.'Second, as of right now,YouTube still doesn't tell you your videos have been demonetized.They don't email you, send you a message...The only way to know is to go in and check your list of videos.If you don't manually check every single video you've made, every day,you won't know if they've been flagged or not.Third—this one is pretty big—unless you're uploading a snuff film or something,you will never know why your video was flagged.They do not give you an explanation,nor do they give you a timestamp where the offending portion is.It's all AI magic.This goes against the basic principles of behavioral learning.You know, actions and consequences?If you're trying to house train a dog,you don't just smack it at random times throughout the day.All you'll have then is a scared dog.If creators don't know why their videos are unacceptable,then they can't fix them!They may as well be cursed!You know, for all the talk I hear of machine learning,I think Google might need some more practice at human learningor even animal first.Now, there's a lot of other specifics,but I feel like those elements combined send a message.I'll come back to that.Now, I realize most of you aren't YouTubers,so I'll just try to briefly run through how this affects people who create videos.If you have less than 10,000 subscribers, you're screwed if this system flags you.If you upload a video and it gets flagged,you probably can't fix it, because it doesn't tell you why it's flagged.And you can't appeal it before going public,because you need at least 1,000 views in seven days for that to happen.But you can't get those viewswithout losing most of your money once it's public,because now you have to wait on the appeal, until you start getting paid.Ask any YouTuber if having their videos demonetizedfor the first 48 hours is a big deal.YouTube has set up a complete catch-22 for you.The only way out is to hope you get bigger.If you're bigger, you have different problems.You have all the same traps of smaller YouTubers,except you can appeal your video before it goes public.Now, that is very helpful,but that's still a delay of probably days, who knows how long,before it's safe to go up.Now, that's okay for me.A lot of my viewers are "Half-Life" fans.They're familiar with delays.In fact, I'm surprised I still have a fanbasewith as long as it takes me to make videos.But what about news channels?This could kneecap them.But on top of that, YouTube has a combo in its back pocket.Besides the advertiser-friendly bot that's on the prowl,don't forget about the copyright infringement bot that's also out there.The best way to combat that is to upload your video privately and unmonetized,then let it simmer for a little bit before you make it public.But now, if you want to be safe,you have to switch gears and set it to unlisted and monetized after that,otherwise you risk losing your money.That's a nice little kill zone they've set up there.As I understand it, anything less than this is playing with fire.Uh-oh...Uh-oh...!Uh-oh!Actually, you may be in trouble anyway.This part is pure speculation,but if you let your video linger unlisted and monetizedfor a day or two and you're in the clear,but then you're flagged after making it public,then... that's game over.There's no defense against that, your channel's done.Now, I don't know if that's how it actually operates—I hope not—but that certainly seems like it's within the realm of possibilities.In summation, making videos and getting paid for itjust got a lot trickier on YouTube.It reminds me of those obstacle courses with the tiresthat you have to step through.But there's more going on here.Even if everything I just said changes and becomes outdated,this next part I think is only going to become more relevant as time goes on.Since YouTube is really stepping up their game to get seriousabout these advertiser-friendly guidelines,what are these guidelines?Well, I took a look at them, and some of them seem sensible,but they paint a larger picture of what's occurring here.Now, just to address the peanut gallery,yes, many of these rules have been in place a long time.However, one of the first things you learn in criminal justice classesis laws are meaningless if they're not enforced.So now that YouTube is really enforcing things, that also carries new meaning.And looking at this, I'm seeing some very large consequences.One is that YouTube is going to become more sanitized.Now, some of this I agree with.I don't come to YouTube to view the most vile stuff on the planet.The problem is some of the most memorable videos I've ever seenand will stick with me forever violate some of these categories.Like one where a prankster pretends to be stealing gas from other people's cars,or another prankster pretends to be a zombiewith an axe killing somebody in a park,or a video documenting the journey of someone traveling across Canadaby illegally stowing away on freight trains.All of these videos have brought sincere joy into my life.The prank ones made me laugh so hard I couldn't breathe, which is rare.I can go years without that happening.And the last one is not only one of the most suspenseful videos I've seen,but it's a journey I consider true performance art.I can't even explain it, but it touched something in my soul.By demonetizing videos like these, we are absolutely losing future art,because it creates a chilling effect as to what kind of content is acceptable.Videos on the fringe will still get made,but there might be ten times as less, because of these changes.Now that's the entertainment side of things, but what about serious topics?This part right here has really large consequences:how controversial topics can be deemed not suitable for advertisers.Traditional media has been dying a slow death, partially out of convenience,but also because YouTubers can talk in depth about topicsthe mainstream news will largely avoid,because they have their own criteria of what to cover, and what not to.For example, one story that didn't get much play by the mainstream newsis there was a study last year that showed 3,000 cities across the countryhave more toxic levels of lead in their water than Flint, Michigan.Well, most of the news already talked about Flint.They didn't need more than one lead in the water story.Why would people want to know that?Well, if you live in the darker-colored or white areas on this map,you could be drinking lead!See, me, I would call that a national emergencyand bears worth repeating ad nauseam.It's not like we fixed it.But that was just a blip for the news, and they moved on.I only found out about it because of some YouTuber talking about it.But this could be considered a controversial and tragic topic,because it is,so that's bound to stir up political bickering, which advertisers don't like,so they walk away from that.This means you're gonna have a less informed populaceabout any important issue that isn't easily monetizable by advertisers.The reason this matters is YouTube is a de facto monopoly.Yes, there are technically other options for hosting video, but not very viable.YouTube is so big that whatever they do has consequences felt across society.Of course, there will be all kinds of videos still getting made,but this points things in a specific direction now.See, mass media has incredible power,because the more you're exposed to one type of message over another,the more that influences your way of thinking.There's a quote from the book "Brave New World" I like that says,"Sixty-two thousand four hundred repetitions make one truth."Now I don't know if that's the number or not,but the point is that the more you repeat the same message over and over again,the more people will think that's reality, whether it is or not.And even if you're resilient to...brainwashing basically, the more you hear the same message,that's still time you're spending thinking about that message.It can frame everything around it.So for a platform as large as YouTubeto be actively deincentivizing controversial material,I think that's going to affect the flow of history.Now I'm sure a lot of you are doubting that this is that significant a change,but if you're on an ocean voyage and you change course just a little bit,you end up in a completely different place!Well, this AI bot is a wave, shifting everything around a little bit.Now it's easy to blame this on big money interests influencing everything,but it kind of is.This all started when a bunch of corporations pulled advertising,because YouTube has over a billion videos on it, and if any of those are offensive,and a generic car commercial appears before it starts,then...that's the end of the world, is my understanding.This cost YouTube hundreds of millions of dollars,so this AI is a knee-jerk response to the problem.I find it almost audacious that after losing all that revenue from advertisers,the official YouTube blog has multiple poststalking about how this is an effort to combat terrorism,with no mention whatsoever about how this is financially motivated.Yeah... that's the main reason YouTube is doing this:to stop the terrorists.Because you go to the front page of YouTube,and all you see is terrorist videos.It's nothing but guys in ski masks chopping people's heads off.So let's set up a system that flags, I don't know...hundreds of millions of videos?To stomp out the terror.That's totally not killing a fly with a sledgehammer.See, crap like this is what keeps "Deus Ex" staying relevant!Never mind that Alphabet, Google's parent companylost a 25 billion market cap in less than a week from YouTube—totally unrelated.And the irony on this gets truly amazingwhen I discovered one of the advertisers that pulled out was HSBC.Remember I said some news stories are more significant than others?Well, a few years ago, HSBC was charged with money laundering for yearsfor all kinds of criminal and terrorist organizations,like the Mexican cartel, Russian mafia, Al-Qaeda, and plenty of others.Well, our amazing Justice Department,despite having truckloads of evidence and a whistleblower,decided to give them a slap on the wrist fine,and nobody lost their license, nobody went to jail.The reasoning from the Justice Department was that HSBC was so bigthat a criminal prosecution would threaten the stability of the economy.The phrase "too big to jail" got popularized from this case.And as a side note,Lanny Breuer, the Attorney General for the criminal division running that,has since gone back to his old firm,where he received a starting salary of four million dollars a year upon return.I'm sure those kinds of connections had no influence on his case decision.The reason I bring all that up isapparently it's okay for an advertiser to fund terrorism,but being associated in a video that brings that up?Whoa, that's a problem.In a different age, executives at HSBC would be in prison right now,and the real debate would be if whether they had committed treason or not,because I can actually see both sides of that argument.And these are some of the people calling the shots on your video being demonetized!And hey, here's another thing I noticed in the guidelines:"inappropriate use of family entertainment characters."So that video where Winnie the Pooh worships Satan is a no-go.Now that struck me as odd, because parody is completely protected under fair use,and can certainly be profitable.The show "Robot Chicken" revolves around the whole concept.Their Swedish Chef skit is, again,another video that has brought me pure joy.But when you have advertisers like Disney,who seem to own almost everything family-friendly these days,you can't have that on YouTube.Now of course, this suppresses creativity,but this rule in particular is a deviationfrom the other more reasonable sounding ones.This says what the big money wants, it's gonna get.Even if you don't think the guidelines are that restrictive,now that these companies know that Google will cave in,what's to stop them from adding new ones in the future?What if saying anything negative about these companiescan get you demonetized in the future?That seems like a logical next step to me.And for everyone saying,we don't know everything that's going on, so we can't judge YouTube,no!You totally can!The very fact that we don't know what's going onis a decision by YouTube itself!I said earlier they're sending a clear message.YouTube appears to have been withholding informationfrom creators that directly affects their livelihood,and even now you have to hunt for it,and then combine that with giving no explanation as to what's wrong,and these are the same tactics you would use if you were running a scamwhere you didn't want people to know what you're doing to them.YouTube, or least management at YouTube knows they're screwing people over!They just want to hide this because it means a smoother operation for them.You don't have to answer the tough questionsif you don't answer any questions.I've heard conspiracy theories that YouTube wants to be the next television,so they're trying to court big media names:Disney, MSNBC, Fox, CNN, and so on,and give them special treatment,while leaving all normal creators by the wayside,because they bring in less direct money for them.I have no idea if that's true or not,but it's certainly compatible with what's happening.If YouTube wanted to be honest,they would tell us this AI is still in development,but they had to roll it out early because they were losing too much money,they'll try their best to sort out the false flaggings,and give an apology.But I'm not sure YouTube even knows how to be honest anymore.A few months back, they released a video addressing concernsabout people being unsubscribed from videos automatically,and their response was basically, "It's not happening."– We take this feedback so seriously.YouTube doesn't unsubscribe people from channels.– That didn't go over too well.I guess telling people what they're seeing with their own eyes is not happeningisn't a very good stance.To this day, it's hard for me to get a reading on these people.I can't tell if they're just pod people who are emptyand will sell whatever line is handed to them,or if they've drank the Kool-Aid and believe what they're saying,because they're so far detached from what's actually happening.It's a tough call.If any of you are good at reading faces, feel free to let me know what you think.So I guess some of you are wondering what does this mean for my videos?Well, nothing good.I'm hesitant to say, "I'll be okay," because I feel like as soon as I do,YouTube will show up and throw me in a van,then you don't hear from me again,but I think I'm gonna survive this round.At least until the next Judgement Day.See, I'm lucky in the sense that I've been hammeredmultiple times already by YouTube,and also by the company Machinima.Boy, nothing YouTube can throw at me will compare to that.They could shut down my whole channel right now,and that would still be better than what I was facing with Machinima.Anyway, I saw this coming years ago.Not this exact event,but I was losing money the same time my views were going up,and no matter how hard I worked, my average was going down.So I made a Beg-A-Thon video as a Hail Mary attemptto try to keep this going about the same way it has been,and you guys utterly saved me.Thanks again for that!Almost entirely since then,I've had to depend more on you guys than on YouTube.Unfortunately, I've had to rely on both,but this means I can glide along slowly when things are getting worse,and I have a lot more time to adapt,whereas income disruptions for the average YouTuberare more like going over a cliff.[screaming]So I'm on fan welfare now.I'm not happy about that,mostly because I don't like having a burden on anyone else.My pride is still a complete non-issue.But I really like the surviving part!I'll try not to screw up too badly.You can even drug test me.Look, the doctor says my blood is good!As for the videos, I think I can do the tire obstacle course,but this does mean a few ideas I have I'm gonna have to hold off on.For example, I've currently appealed all my videos that have been flagged,except "Doom Guy's Mind."I think that one might be a tough sell.Regardless, I have a giant pool of ideas,so I should be able to keep going if they don't turn the screws further.Honestly, my "career" on YouTube feels like I've survivedmultiple rounds of Russian Roulette.So far, the chambers have been coming up empty...This is just the latest round where a few people at the table next to mehad their brains blown out.I mean, this bot is gonna kill some channels, I have no doubt.Actually, Russian Roulette isn't the best analogybecause that implies I'm unscathed.I've definitely taken a few rounds in the arm metaphorically,but my brains are still good!So, more videos are coming. YouTube still hasn't killed me.So this final part is for people of the future,so you can see how right or wrong I am.I think the real big picture of these YouTube changesis that YouTubers are feeling more and more what most people are.It's getting trickier to earn a living across most fields.Did you know that 94% of the jobs created since the start of the recessionhave been temp or contract jobs?That doesn't sound like stability to me!Or hey, Millennials, which I guess means me too.I'm not sure what I am.Did you know that we're earning20% less than the baby boomers did when they were our age,and have 50% less wealth?That's kind of a lot!And speaking of the recession, my understanding iswe've done almost nothing to prevent that from happening again in some other flavor.I mean, we've removed the main regulation put into place after the Great Depressionto prevent another Great Depression from ever happening again.I'm not sure why we did that.I think the system we're in is slowly falling apart.Almost 2/3 of Americans are living from paycheck to paycheck,and can't handle a $500 expense without going into debt.I could be missing something,but that is not what financial stability looks like to me.Hell, even Google was found guilty of colludingto keep wages down on their own employees.Got to make up the cost of those terrorist videos somehow.And by "the system,"I mean the concept that the average person can get a job that pays okay,and they can get by without having to choose betweenpaying for medication or paying rent.I think that's slowly eroding.I mentioned in my robot jobs video,which hey, was not flagged,that we're entering an erawhere there's going to be less jobs that pay enough to get by,than there are people who need them.On the grand scale, this round of YouTube changesis just one of many cracks being exposed.See, it's a loop.My generation makes less money, so that means we have less to spend,which means ads aren't as effective,so Google needs to squeeze things harder in order to maintain that ad revenue,which means we get less money!I think this is only gonna get worse.Now you might think,well hey, more people will just get supported on Patreonor take donations like me and be okay.Yeah, maybe.But then YouTube doesn't get its cut,and ultimately, they're the ones hosting the site,so that means they're gonna take more and more measures to turn a profit.Honestly, part of me doesn't understand how YouTube even works.I mean I get the concept, but what, we just keep adding storage space forever?There's four or five hundred hours of video uploaded every minute.We just keep doing that to infinity?That's the plan?Maybe YouTube's using those petabyte discs I heard about.Those can hold a lot.I remember reading a comment in a forum where a guy sayshe just uploads a video of himself eating lunch every day for years,just to test the limits.Thanks?I think more changes are coming to YouTube.So in conclusion, everything's going to hell in slow motion,do whatever you can to survive.My view is biased, but that's because I'm on YouTube.Okay, that is it for serious talk.Except the stop killing games thing, I'll do more on that later.I want somebody else discussing the serious stuff.All this reality just makes me want to dive further into escapism.My last video was talking about orcs, the next one's gonna have time travel.That's closer to where I want to keep things.I'll just say this:I've known a girl before who didn't like anything offensive in movies;no unpleasantness at all.It really limited what she wanted to watch.Her dad said that her ideal movie would be happy people singingabout how happy they are.Well, Brianne, I think you're gonna like the direction YouTube is heading.[Subtitles by Erasmus Magnus]♪♪Come on, come on...[pellet vanishes]Oh, what the hell YouTube?!

title: Animation on Youtube MIGHT BE OVER!
description:
YouTube has gone full psycho mode on Storytime animators

Massive channels are getting shadowbanned. Storytime animators are waking up to find their entire channel demonetized overnight  no warning, no real explanation, just an automated "appeal denied"

So I went digging to figure out what's actually going on, why it's happening, who's at risk, and whether animation on YouTube can even survive it.

Spoiler: it's YouTube's AI moderation system trying to fight AI slop content... and failing so badly it's taking real human creators down as collateral damage.

If you want to help animators who've been hit by this, the best thing you can do costs nothing: watch their videos all the way through, like, comment, and let the algorithm know their work is worth pushing. It genuinely makes a difference.

Thanks for watching 
if this made you as frustrated as it made me, share it around. 

#YouTubeAnimator #Shadowban #Demonetized #AIonYouTube #StorytimeAnimation #CreatorEconomy

My entire channel has been officially demonetized due to entire YouTube found out that my channel was removed from my channel.What the is going on? Since YouTube might think that this video is AI simply because it's animated.I first heard about all this about two weeks ago. I was getting my daily dose of brain routine when I noticed that Shozy, a storytime animator that I love watching, made this video. I received an email from YouTube saying how from that day my channel had lost all monetization out of nowhere. Basically, he woke up to find that his entire channel had gotten demonetized with zero prior warning. And that means he can no longer earn money from any of his videos, past, present, or future. And that scared the out of me. And what was even scarier was YouTube's whole reasoning for doing this to him in the first place. Misleading family content. Content that intentionally or unintentionally could attract young minors and families, but contains mature themes such as sexual content or violence. Now, let me explain why this is bull. You see, every time you upload a video, YouTube will ask you if the content you're uploading is made for kids or not. And most people like Shy will tell YouTube, "No, this video is not made for kids." So, how the is this misleading kids if you already told YouTube that it's not made for kids? What the? So, he appeals it. And at this point, the channel is supposed to get revealed by an actual human being in the back end who then go through his videos before getting back to him. So, you'd expect this whole process to like take a couple of days or something, right? They got back to him in an hour. He yeah he he instantly got denied by an automated response basically telling him to go eat fix your channel and try appealing again in 3 months you as you can imagine being an aspiring YouTube animator myself I went from being scared toing horrified so I got digging and it turns out he wasn't the only one everywhere I looked so many other animators were going through the same exact thing animated honoring Godzilla is animations.This channel is cool as it's not just story time animators. So many of the faces animation channels started noticing a natural dips in the views starting a few months back. And I'm not sure if it's because of AI or because of cultural trends within AI. So at this point you're probably wondering why why is YouTube selfmutilating by killing some of the most passionate and hardworking creators who objectively make the platform what it is. Do I have an answer? No. But I do have a theory. If you spent any time on the site over the past two years or so, then the reason is probably pretty obvious. AI slop content. Like the site is just infested with so many AI content farms pooping out cheap inauthentic content in order to gain the system and make a ton of money while doing so. And I'm sorry to hop on it so much, but this is just everywhere, dude. It's like a plague or like a cancer that just refuses to die. And I'll explain what I mean in a minute, but how I see it, these crazy new actions that are affecting actual hardworking human creators is most likely YouTube having copious amounts of chemo trying to get rid of the tumors. But if you're going to build a system to fight cheap, mass-produced content, then you better make damn sure that you can tell the difference between some dude pressing a button to get a machine to do all the work for him and animators spending weeks of their time, energy, and HP to make a single YouTube video, at least before you implement it into the damn platform. title: Google Ads Limited Ad Serving? How to Fix It (2026 Guide)
description:
Is your Google Ads account getting fewer impressions due to the "Limited Ad Serving" policy? Learn exactly why Google restricts unqualified advertisers and the 3 steps you can take today to lift these limits and protect your campaign reach.

If your ad impressions suddenly dropped, Google’s Limited Ad Serving policy might be the culprit. To protect users from poor experiences and potential abuse, Google automatically limits ads that are too generic, reference other brands without permission, or come from unverified accounts.

In this video, we break down what triggers these restrictions and how to become a "qualified advertiser" with a strong track record of policy compliance and trust. We also show you a quick, actionable setup trick to clarify your brand relationship directly inside Responsive Search Ads (RSAs).

🛠️ Key Steps to Become a Qualified Advertiser
• Build Clear Creatives: Ensure a transparent brand relationship in your ad copy.
• Pin Your Domain: In your Google Ads account, edit your Responsive Search Ad, click the Pin icon next to your domain, and select "Show only in position 1."
• Complete Verification: Finish your Advertiser Verification program as soon as you are prompted.
• Maintain Compliance: Keep a clean history with Google's advertising policies to build account maturity.

description:

computer.Speak prompts directly into the app,using voice to text to talk through concepts or troubleshoot questions.Attach specific videos or shorts from your channel to get targeted comment summaries,retention diagnostics, or follow up ideasand conversations automatically sync between mobile and desktopso you can keep the conversation going no matter what device you're working on.Imagine you could add visual context to your chats on Ask Studio, Mobile,and Desktop by uploading thumbnail concepts, screenshots,or sketches to brainstorm and create even faster.To get started, just hit the plus attachment button on the bottomleft corner of your chat box.For thumbnail ideation, you can upload up to ten images at once, including sketches,mood boards, or graphics to generate new conceptsand compare thumbnail variants side by side.You can also upload still frames from your work in progress.Edit to get targeted notes on framing composition before exporting uploaded images.Stay strictly private to your active sessionand are automatically deleted after 30 days.What if the old trends tab turned into a brand new research tab on desktop?A personalized content first feed built to help you exploreand validate ideas before you start creating.And with this new research tab,you could spot breakout outlier videos across your niche that are significantlyoutperforming a channel's normal baseline,like five X outlier score and really resonating with audiences.Filter your audience to narrow results by format like videos or shorts, duration,and watch by my viewersto see what your existing audience is already enjoying across YouTube.And the research tab connects directly to Ask Studio,so you can summarize recurring title patternsand packaging strategies behind those top breakout videos.YouTube analytics is becoming insights, shifting from dense, raw data to clear,plain language takeaways that explain the why behind the metrics.Accessible directly from the left navigation menuand studio on desktop insights include streamlined layouts with metrics groupedinto scannable shelves on your overview page,cutting visual clutter while keeping key numbers front and center,and ask Studio Card for eligible creators.Breaking down key channel trends, top video drivers and audience behavior,and for us analytics nerds,detailed tables and custom date ranges just a title: Chucky (MrBeast) on Dynamic Thumbnails, Video A/B, and the YouTube Algorithm

02:44 - Why intros are part of video packaging

06:56 - Video A/B testing for Shorts
09:15 - Advice for creators overwhelmed by testing
11:36 - The risk of A/B testing worse options
13:50 - Introducing dynamic thumbnails and audience clusters
17:10 - When thumbnails without Jimmy's face win

40:44 - Learning from failure and long-term growth
